items.title: Sea otters, kelp forests, and the extinction of Steller's sea cow
items.who: J. A. Estes, A. Burdin and D. F. Doak
items.note: Argues that otter removal and the resulting loss of kelp could have contributed to the sea cow's decline alongside direct hunting.

items.title: The dilemma of trade samples and the importance of museum vouchers: caveats from a study on the extinction of Steller's sea cow
items.who: N. D. Pyenson, J. F. Parham and J. Velez-Juarbe
items.note: Questions the provenance of bone samples behind Crerar et al.'s (2014) claim of a medieval St Lawrence Island population, as they came through trade rather than vouchered collections.

items.title: Inferring extinction in North American and Hawaiian birds in the presence of sighting uncertainty
items.who: D. L. Roberts and I. Jarić
items.note: Re-estimates extinction dates for North American and Hawaiian birds with methods that weight certain and uncertain sightings differently.

items.title: On the functional extinction of the Passenger Pigeon
items.who: D. L. Roberts, I. Jarić and A. R. Solow
items.note: Compares the dates of the last egg and skin specimens and finds no evidence that the species stopped breeding long before its final extinction.

items.title: An 'Aukward' Tale: A Genetic Approach to Discover the Whereabouts of the Last Great Auks
items.who: J. E. Thomas et al.
items.note: Matches mitochondrial genomes from the preserved organs of the 1844 Eldey pair to candidate skins and identifies the male in Brussels.

items.title: Lazarus ecology: Recovering the distribution and migratory patterns of the extinct Carolina parakeet
items.who: K. R. Burgio, C. J. Carlson and M. W. Tingley
items.note: Combines historical accounts and museum specimens in distribution models, finding a smaller range than assumed and different niches for the two subspecies.

items.title: Natural selection shaped the rise and fall of passenger pigeon genomic diversity
items.who: G. G. R. Murray et al.
items.note: Genomes from 41 birds indicate a consistently large population, contradicting the argument that natural population instability primed the collapse.

items.title: Georeferenced sighting and specimen occurrence data of the extinct Carolina Parakeet (Conuropsis carolinensis) from 1564 - 1944
items.who: K. R. Burgio, C. J. Carlson and A. L. Bond
items.note: Open georeferenced database of parakeet sightings and specimens, largely built on Daniel McKinley's searches of historical texts.

items.title: Can genomic variation explain the extinction of the passenger pigeon?
items.who: C.-M. Hung, R. M. Zink and S.-H. Li
items.note: Reply defending the view that population fluctuations, not only hunting, made the pigeon vulnerable.

items.title: Demographic reconstruction from ancient DNA supports rapid extinction of the great auk
items.who: J. E. Thomas et al.
items.note: Finds no genetic sign of decline before intensive hunting from the sixteenth century and shows hunting alone could account for extinction.

items.title: Evolutionary History, Genomic Adaptation to Toxic Diet, and Extinction of the Carolina Parakeet
items.who: P. Gelabert et al.
items.note: Genome of a museum specimen shows no long prior decline or recent inbreeding, suggesting an abrupt extinction attributable to human causes.

items.title: The Dodo and the Red Hen, A Saga of Extinction, Misunderstanding, and Name Transfer: A Review
items.who: A. S. Cheke and J. C. Parish
items.note: Argues the undescribed 'dodaarsen' of the 1680s were probably red hens, so the dodo disappeared unobserved earlier than statistical estimates suggest.

items.title: Steller's sea cow genome suggests this species began going extinct before the arrival of Paleolithic humans
items.who: F. S. Sharko et al.
items.note: Low heterozygosity in the Commander Islands population suggests a long natural decline before eighteenth-century hunting finished the species.

items.title: The two extinctions of the Carolina Parakeet Conuropsis carolinensis
items.who: K. R. Burgio et al.
items.note: Estimates that the western subspecies died out around 1914 and the eastern one in the late 1930s or mid-1940s, decades after the last captive bird.

items.title: The great auk in Norway: From common to locally extinct
items.who: A. K. Hufthammer and K. O. Hufthammer
items.note: Study of 477 bones from 53 Norwegian sites suggesting the bird vanished from southern Scandinavia before 4000 years ago.

items.title: The Complete Genome Sequence of Conuropsis carolinensis, the Carolina Parakeet
items.who: T. Hains, S. Pirro et al.
items.note: Publicly released whole genome from a captive individual, deposited in GenBank for comparative work.

items.title: The Last of the Great Auks: Oral History and Ritual Killings at St Kilda
items.who: A. Fleming
items.note: Weighs conflicting accounts of the 'last' British great auk killed c. 1840 and concludes two birds were probably killed at St Kilda.

items.title: The Last of Its Kind: The Search for the Great Auk and the Discovery of Extinction
items.who: G. Pálsson
items.note: Study of Wolley and Newton's Garefowl Books as a record of the last hunters and of how extinction became thinkable.

items.title: Inferring species extinction from sighting data
items.who: R. S. McCrea, T. Cheale, E. Campillo-Funollet and D. L. Roberts
items.note: Review of sighting-record extinction methods and their assumptions, released with an R Shiny application implementing several of them.

items.title: The hunt for the last great auks: ancient DNA resolves a 180-year-old mystery
items.who: E. L. Cavill, J. E. Thomas et al.
items.venue: Zoological Journal of the Linnean Society
items.note: Ancient DNA, letters and sale records identify the female of the 1844 Eldey pair as the skin at the Cincinnati Museum Center.

items.title: Additional records of the extinct Carolina Parakeet Conuropsis carolinensis
items.who: B. E. Leese, A. L. Bond et al.
items.venue: Bulletin of the British Ornithologists' Club
items.note: Adds 131 newly compiled and 81 newly georeferenced historical records, bringing the known total to 555.
